briefings.title: Chelsea Finn: This is the State of the Art in Robotics
briefings.tldr: Chelsea Finn, co-founder of Physical Intelligence, explains how the robotics industry is entering its "GPT era" by moving from task-specific models to general-purpose foundation models (like PIO7) that achieve long-term autonomy through reinforcement learning, memory, and diverse data.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Chelsea Finn, co-founder of Physical Intelligence, explains how the robotics industry is entering its "GPT era" by moving from task-specific models to general-purpose foundation models (like PIO7) that achieve long-term autonomy through reinforcement learning, memory, and diverse data.

## 1. The Reliability & Long-Term Autonomy Problem
* **The High Stakes of Physical AI:** Unlike traditional machine learning applications (product recommendations or ad ranking) where human customers act as a safety net against model mistakes, physical AI systems must make direct, autonomous decisions in the real world with minimal human oversight.
* **The Espresso Benchmark:** Achieving high utility requires reliability—such as operating an espresso machine at over 90% reliability to avoid constant human babysitting.
* **Long-Horizon Kitchen Task (10–15 Minutes):** 
  * **Short-Term Video Memory:** Uses 10 seconds of video memory computed efficiently.
  * **Long-Term Text Memory:** Summarizes past history (spanning 10–15 minutes) into compressed text to track progress across sequential steps (wiping counters, putting away mustard, washing dishes).

## 2. Scalable Reinforcement Learning for Robotics
* **Overcoming Dead-End Trajectories:** Traditional RL algorithms waste physical robot time on dead ends (e.g., trying to fold two jammed cardboard boxes together). Physical Intelligence uses human teleoperation interventions to early-terminate or correct episodes and teach recovery.
* **General-Purpose Value Functions:** Instead of computing numerous rollouts per prompt, they train a general-purpose value function on diverse robot experience videos to predict success/failure timeframes across entirely different workflows (e.g., shirt folding vs. fridge retrieval).
* **Throughput and Success Gains:** 
  * **2x Throughput Increase:** Achieved in cardboard box construction, labeling, and stacking workflows after applying the RL post-training stage.
  * **>90% Success Rate:** Achieved on the espresso-making task.
  * **13-Hour Continuous Run:** Demonstrated long-term autonomy on a latte-making workflow combining robot espresso-dispensing and human milk-steaming.

## 3. General-Purpose Foundation Models (PI0)
* **Moving Beyond Custom Datasets:** Transitioning from training bespoke models from scratch for every individual project to using out-of-the-box generalist models.
* **Detailed Prompting & Heterogeneous Data:** The PIO7 foundation model ingests extremely diverse data (low-quality robot demos, policy rollouts, human videos, and web data) using detailed prompting:
  * **Metadata Prompting:** Signals episode length and data quality, which uniquely *improves* model performance when adding low-quality data (whereas unprompted models degrade).
  * **Subtask Instructions & Subgoal Images:** Conditioned via a high-level policy and world model.
* **Performance Parity:** Out-of-the-box pre-trained PIO7 models match or outperform fine-tuned specialist models (PIV6) across tasks like coffee making and box building.

## 4. Compositional Generalization in Robotics
* **Zero-Shot Air Fryers:** Demonstrated the ability to interact with rare appliances (air fryers) with virtually zero air-fryer data in the pre-training set.
* **Cross-Robot Transfer:** Successfully transferred clothing-folding skills to a completely different industrial robot platform (a barm robot with different linkages, joint configurations, and size) without any robot-specific folding training data.
* **Data Diversity Importance:** Ablation studies confirm that removing the most diverse data causes performance on held-out tasks to drop dramatically.

## Notable Quotes
> "If we think about physical AI that are actually operating in the physical world, they have to be directly making decisions that affect the physical world. And this means that they're far more useful when they're operating fully autonomously."
> — **Chelsea Finn**

> "We really firmly have physical intelligence in the right side of this timeline. We're kind of firmly more in like a GPT and Dolly-like era for robotics and physical intelligence."
> — **Chelsea Finn**

briefings.title: How to find businesses with (almost) zero competition
briefings.tldr: Sam Parr and Shaan Puri explore hidden-in-plain-sight business models—such as lab-testing monkeys and soybean oil collateral audits—while discussing how entrepreneurs can find low-competition opportunities through childhood passions, curiosity, and the art of noticing.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Sam Parr and Shaan Puri explore hidden-in-plain-sight business models—such as lab-testing monkeys and soybean oil collateral audits—while discussing how entrepreneurs can find low-competition opportunities through childhood passions, curiosity, and the art of noticing.

## Hidden-in-Plain-Sight Businesses & High-Margin Niches
* **Lab Testing Monkeys:** 
  * More than 20% of all drugs are tested on monkeys, utilizing roughly tens of thousands of imported monkeys annually (specifically long-tailed cynomolgus macaques).
  * Monkey prices surged from roughly $2,000 to between $20,000 and $50,000 per monkey following COVID-19 and China halting exports.
  * **Charles River Labs:** A major publicly traded research testing-as-a-service provider working with ~80% of biotech companies, doing $4 billion a year in revenue; they purchased a monkey breeding supply business for $500 million to control supply chains.
* **The Soybean Oil Crisis & Audit Arbitrage:** 
  * Warren Express/American Express history: A massive financial scandal erupted when a fraudster took multi-million-dollar loans using non-existent soybean oil inventory (tanks filled with seawater) backed by American Express verification guarantees.
  * The scale of such hidden service industries demonstrates that massive multi-hundred-million-dollar businesses operate in obscure nooks and crannies far from traditional software and tech.
* **Dental Back-Office Automation:**
  * **Daydream Dental:** Founded by a Stanford grad/dropout whose mother was a dentist, the company uses AI and human teams to handle dental insurance billing codes and claims.
  * They collect 15% to 20% more revenue for dentists that would otherwise be left on the table, scaling to close to $10 million a year in revenue by year two.
* **Industrial Generator Servicing:** 
  * Companies servicing and installing industrial-sized generators for nursing homes and hospitals represent vital, low-competition, high-defensibility infrastructure businesses.

## The Art of Notice & Entrepreneurial Advantage
* **Studying Creativity over Hustle:** 
  * Shaan Puri notes that studying creative icons (like Rick Rubin or top comedians) reveals that great insights come from **noticing** everyday struggles rather than brute-force scaling.
  * **Jerry Seinfeld's Daily Habit:** Seinfeld has spent the first 2 hours of every day for 40 years writing half-jokes on legal pads, compiling them into his book *Is This Anything?*.
* **Paul Graham's "How to Do Great Work" Framework:**
  * **Motor and Rudder:** Follow the path of most excitement because genuine interest provides both work endurance and differentiation.
  * **The Frontier:** Travel to the absolute edge of any field or industry to discover unaddressed gaps and tedious problems that smart people normally ignore.
* **Playing in Low-Competition Pools:** 
  * Avoid crowded, high-status fields (like building standard to-do list apps or entering hyper-competitive gaming championships) and instead target obscure categories with weak competition.

## Childhood Roots & Shameless Enthusiasm
* **Knowing Thy 8-Year-Old Self:**
  * Childhood free time and early obsessions provide a blueprint for genuine adult interests (e.g., Dan Brown's father giving him treasure maps for Christmas, leading directly to writing *The Da Vinci Code*).
* **Embrace Shamelessness:**
  * **Elan Lee (Exploding Kittens):** Creator of multiple top-10 board games globally, building massive commercial success by leaning fully into childhood toys, LEGO building, and escape rooms without filtering out his "grown man kid" interests.
  * **Enthusiasm as a Superpower:** While smart people often feel self-conscious or low-status being enthusiastic, genuine enthusiasm is a magnetic honeypot that attracts like-minded collaborators and provides the resilience needed for hard work.

## Awe, San Francisco, and Obsession
* **The Emotion of Awe in San Francisco:**
  * Sam Parr spent 7 days in San Francisco, noting that the city induces **awe**—experiencing vastness that forces mental schema adaptation, which reduces anxiety and self-rumination by shifting focus outward.
* **San Francisco's Quirky Startup Culture:**
  * The city fosters outlier, quirky, and counter-culture founders working on unusual, high-variance ideas (such as robots making Fettuccine Alfredo) that differ sharply from execution-heavy media businesses in New York.
* **True Crime & Code Fidelity:**
  * Shaan Puri highlights *The Art Thief*, a true story of a criminal who stole $3 billion worth of art strictly to experience it in his bedroom rather than profit from it, driven by a childhood metal-detecting background.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Everything is a business. It would not exist if there wasn't a entrepreneur behind it making it exist. And the world is full of these projects and everywhere... It's always bigger than you think."* — Sam Parr

> *"Go into a category that is just not ripe with really smart, you know, high agency people, and you're playing against weak competition."* — Shaan Puri

> *"Imagine there was another game that had the same prize pool as the world Fortnite championship, but there's only seven players. Like, you know, that's what happens with some of these traits like noticing."* — Shaan Puri

briefings.title: Inside America’s Million-Drone Factory
briefings.tldr: Neros Technologies operates a new 250,000-square-foot "Millennium One" facility designed to scale production to one million drones per year, currently manufacturing over 250 drones daily under one roof.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Neros Technologies operates a new 250,000-square-foot "Millennium One" facility designed to scale production to one million drones per year, currently manufacturing over 250 drones daily under one roof. Co-Founder & CEO Soren Monroe-Anderson and host Molly O'Shea tour the factory floors, detailing end-to-end engineering, automated tracking, and aggressive in-house vertical integration.

## Facility Overview & Scaling
* **Millennium One Facility:** 
  * **Scale and Footprint:** A 250,000-square-foot factory designed to eliminate multiple-site logistics and reach a target capacity of one million drones per year — a massive upgrade from their previous 15,000-square-foot facility with 100 people.
  * **Unified Operations:** Houses engineering, testing, supply chain, manufacturing, and future component expansion under one roof to ensure tight, cross-functional collaboration.
* **Current Production Metrics:** 
  * **Output Volume:** Manufacturing a little over 250 drones per day at normal operating rates.
  * **Facility Highlights:** Features a massive 30x60-foot American flag (noted as the largest in the South Bay) and an in-house powerlifting gym for employees.

## Engineering Labs & R&D
* **Flight Test & Prototyping Teams:** 
  * **Development Testing:** A 10-person flight test team operates out in the desert roughly two hours away, typically running two teams in separate locations every single day to push prototypes to failure.
  * **Testing Hardware:** Racks of engineering development drones and survivability-tested Archer AI drones are constantly pushed to their limits.
* **Bandit Interceptor Development:** 
  * **Performance Progress:** V1 Bandit interceptors reached about 300 km/h (roughly 40 km/h faster than earlier iterations) after just a couple of months of development.
  * **Future Benchmark:** Targeting roughly 400 km/h to effectively intercept faster jet-powered Shahed variants using bigger motors, larger batteries, and improved aerodynamics.
* **Design & Manufacturing Philosophy:** 
  * **Airframe Construction:** Uses 2D-cut carbon plates for cheap, lightweight mass manufacturing, pairing aluminum bottom plates with thermal interface material to act as a motherboard heat sink.
  * **Rejection of Battlefield 3D Printing:** Dismisses battlefield 3D printing for core components (circuit boards, motors, radios), noting that true mass manufacturing requires efficient, centralized factories rather than field printing.

## Assembly Lines & Manufacturing Software
* **Production Line Layout:** 
  * **Station Design:** Features side-by-side manual assembly lines for drones and ground stations, equipped with preloaded part bins and preset-torque drivers to ease operator burden.
  * **Software Tracking:** Manufacturing software deployed across tablets tracks serial numbers of critical components and logs station completion times to identify bottlenecks.
* **Automation Strategy:** 
  * **Manual vs. Automated:** Current drone versions are not designed around automation, making manual stations ideal for rapid iteration; full automation will require a ground-up product redesign.

## Testing & New Product Introduction (NPI)
* **100% End-of-Line Flight Testing:** 
  * **Stress Testing:** Every single manufactured drone undergoes 100% flight testing with a payload to simulate high-stress conditions.
  * **Data Collection:** Automated pre-test stations screen for issues, with long-term data collection aimed at eventually reducing flight testing to sample testing.
* **New Product Introduction (NPI) Line:** 
  * **Archer AI Line:** A dedicated NPI space larger than their entire old production line is currently used to prep the Archer AI product for mass production later this year.
  * **In-House Expansion:** Massive open factory space is reserved for bringing component manufacturing in-house to achieve complete vertical integration.

## Notable Quotes
> "We sized this building to be big enough to do a million drones per year. In our previous facility, we had 100 people and manufacturing in 15,000 square feet. We were just fighting to even get drones out the door."  
> — Soren Monroe-Anderson
> 
> "To go after jet-powered Shahed drones we need to be closer to like 400 km/h. So that would be kind of the ideal end state."  
> — Soren Monroe-Anderson
> 
> "My hottest take is that a lot of the defense tech, maybe the majority of defense tech products that are being put out right now by startups are not very effective and maybe even like completely useless... They're fake."  
> — Soren Monroe-Anderson

briefings.title: Khabib Nurmagomedov: Dagestan, MMA, UFC, Islam, Conor, Fedor & Football | Lex Fridman Podcast #500
briefings.tldr: Undefeated UFC legend Khabib Nurmagomedov reflects on how his father's rigorous discipline, the unforgiving conditions of Dagestan, and an unyielding hatred of losing forged his 29-0 career.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Undefeated UFC legend Khabib Nurmagomedov reflects on how his father's rigorous discipline, the unforgiving conditions of Dagestan, and an unyielding hatred of losing forged his 29-0 career. He discusses the fine line between championship glory and the corrupting traps of fame, his lifelong passion for football and Real Madrid, and how his Islamic faith keeps him grounded amid immense global success.

## Foundations of Excellence: Dagestan and the Spartan Gyms
* **The Spartan Origin:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** explains that before opening a modern Makhachkala facility in 2019, athletes trained in a simple school gym with mats, a single punching bag, and one climbing rope, sharing just one cold-water shower among 70 people. 
* **The Father's Role:** His father built an at-home gym in their village of Sildi and Kirovaul, serving as the primary coach whose voice and drilling sounds provided Khabib's earliest childhood memories.
* **The Value of Struggle:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** argues that comfort is the enemy of champions, noting that wealthy families statistically never produce fighters who willingly endure daily injuries and exhaustion. Hunger and harsh environments are required to forge elite competitors.
* **Historical Resilience:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** notes that Dagestan's geography—wedged between the Caucasus mountains and the Caspian Sea near Derbent (Babul Abwab)—forced generations to constantly fight invading empires (Khazars, Arabs, Persians, Mongols, Russians) to survive, embedding fighting into the region's culture and blood.

## Championship Mindset: The Psychology of Dominance
* **The Hatred of Losing:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** reveals that his primary fuel was not just wanting to win, but a fierce, addiction-like hatred of losing and panic over missing a single training session.
* **Fanatical Preparation:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** trained 4 to 5 hours every single day, often sneaking out at night to do a third session on the beach when his father wasn't watching. He states that to stand out from hundreds of thousands of people with the same goal, an athlete must take a fanatical approach.
* **Handling Fame and Distractions:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** warns that money, media, flights, and video shoots distract champions and cause them to fall from the top fast. He notes that out of hundreds of thousands of applicants over 35 years of MMA, only a tiny fraction (perhaps 50 true champions) reach and sustain the summit.
* **Grounding Through Religion:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** credits his Islamic faith and his strict father with keeping him humble, emphasizing that powerful people cannot even control basic bodily functions and will all ultimately end up in a grave two meters deep.

## MMA Legends and Greatness: Pride Era, Fedor, and Rivalries
* **The Golden Era of Pride FC:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** cites Mauricio "Shogun" Rua, Fedor Emelianenko, and Georges St-Pierre as his gold standards during the Pride FC era of the 2000s, admiring Shogun's relentless striking and soccer kicks.
* **The Fedor Encounter:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** recalls the 2004 Dagestan Open Combat Sambo Championship where a 15-year-old Khabib watched reigning Pride champion Fedor Emelianenko quietly warm up and drink tea from a thermos, serving as a massive early inspiration.
* **The Conor McGregor Rivalry:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** describes his 2018 fight against Conor McGregor as a cultural event that transcended sports, fueled by personal and religious insults. Despite the massive media pressure, Khabib maintained absolute cool-headed control by relying on a single grounding phone call from his father before the bout.
* **Daniel Cormier's Unique Resume:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** praises two-time Olympian Daniel Cormier as a once-in-a-lifetime athlete who won a Strikeforce Grand Prix and held UFC titles in two weight divisions while pushing fierce rivals like Jon Jones.
* **Islam Makhachev's Rise:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** highlights Islam Makhachev as one of his father's favorite and most disciplined students, noting that Islam maintained a 23-year generational chain of excellence by staying in the gym's uncomfortable "black room" for over a decade.
* **UFC Business Genius:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** praises Dana White as a cold-blooded, brilliant businessman who successfully separated personal relationships from the UFC, building a global brand in 30 years that took other sports 150 years to achieve.

## Football Passions: Real Madrid, Rivalries, and Charisma
* **Childhood Football Roots:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** recalls watching the 1996 Euros (Germany vs. England) and falling permanently in love with Real Madrid during the 1998 Champions League final watched with his father.
* **Cristiano Ronaldo vs. Lionel Messi:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** calls Cristiano Ronaldo a natural-born athlete whose 15-year dominance under immense pressure at Manchester United and Real Madrid is unmatched. While acknowledging Real Madrid's rivalry with Barcelona, he insists that neither Messi nor Ronaldo would have reached their historic heights without each other pushing them for 20 years.
* **Defining Charisma:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** defines football charisma through players like Zinedine Zidane, Ronaldo Nazário, David Beckham, and Edgar Davids—players who possessed an unavoidable energy and took the initiative rather than hiding from the ball.

## Faith, Purpose, and Legacy
* **The Eternal Perspective:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** states that his entire daily routine is structured around his five daily prayers (*Salah*), emphasizing that human beings are servants of God meant to prepare for the Day of Judgment rather than getting corrupted by temporary wealth.
* **Wealth in the Hands, Not the Heart:** **Khabib Nurmagomedov** advises that money is safe to have as long as it stays in your hands to help family and the needy, but once it enters your heart, it corrupts you.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* *No genuine forward-looking predictions, timelines, or future targets regarding specific upcoming events or market metrics were stated in this transcript.*

## Notable Quotes
> *"The best results are born out of the worst conditions. When you live too well, let's say, you're never in need... This is where you need that hunger. You have to be in a position where you are truly in need."* — Khabib Nurmagomedov

> *"We are just not some kind of big, important people here who just decide and get to control everything. We don't get to do that... Either way, they put us all in the exact same grave, you know, two meters down."* — Khabib Nurmagomedov

> *"The tongue speaks what the heart is full of... I just like praising the Almighty and giving all the credit for my success back to Him because everything we have is given to us by the Almighty."* — Khabib Nurmagomedov

briefings.title: Post-Training Is How You Keep Your Taste | Fireworks CEO Lin Qiao
briefings.tldr: Post-training allows companies to embed their unique judgment and taste into AI models after achieving product-market fit, serving as both a strategic moat and a 5–10x cost reduction mechanism for production serving.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Post-training allows companies to embed their unique judgment and taste into AI models after achieving product-market fit, serving as both a strategic moat and a 5–10x cost reduction mechanism for production serving.

## Industry Context & The Shift Toward Owning Intelligence
- **Evolution of Application Development:** Software development has collapsed from taking tens of product engineers and PMs across multiple quarters to a single person building in a few weeks without writing a single line of code, shifting focus from off-the-shelf black-box APIs to building deeper moats.
- **The Value of "Taste":** Every company exists to solve unique problems with its own judgment, taste, and conviction; building on generic APIs risks losing that differentiation.
- **What "Owning Your Intelligence" Means:** 
  - **Data:** Curing production data with high quality and generating synthetic data to enrich it.
  - **Model Weights:** Building on top of existing models and owning the weights using tailored, interoperable techniques.
  - **Serving & Optimization:** Running AB testing to verify product metrics, then feeding insights back into the loop.
- **Audience Breakdown & Engagement Models:** 
  - *Deep Researchers (e.g., Cursor, Cognition):* Want extreme results and control over every knob, using lowest-level APIs with direct RL rollouts and fully controlled trainers.
  - *Product/ML Engineers:* Want high-level control via training SDKs and close iteration with Fireworks' researchers.

## The Post-Training Progression
- **Phase 1: Prompting** – Few-shot prompts used as-is for minutes of interaction to quickly test ideas.
- **Phase 2: RAG & Context Engineering** – Grounding AI usage into your own data for hours of interaction; ideal when factual data is dynamic and constantly changing.
- **Phase 3: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)** – Taking a few hours of data to reflect personalized taste, product choice, or correct structural/behavioral output issues.
- **Phase 4: Preference Tuning (DPO)** – Collecting user interaction data (thumbs-up, thumbs-down) to help models learn product taste and user preferences.
- **Phase 5: Reinforcement Learning (RL)** – Building domain expertise (legal, finance, healthcare, customer support, recruiting, marketing, sales) when models are weak on specific, complex problems.
- **Phase 6: Distillation** – Training a smaller student model via a teacher model to make serving faster and 5–10x more economical (applicable to LLMs, VLMs, and image generation models).

## Common Pitfalls in Post-Training
- **Data Quantity vs. Quality:** Throwing raw data at training does not guarantee great outcomes; data quality must be controlled, with the product team acting as the ultimate judge of quality.
- **Vibe Evals vs. Systematic Evals:** Relying on "vibe checking" founder sentiment instead of systematic unit and integration tests (similar to traditional software development).
- **Sloppy RL Environments:** Building simulations that fail to reflect reality, leading models to hill-climb on bad simulations.
- **Reward Hacking:** Models finding unintended shortcuts to meet optimization goals (e.g., generating zero lines of code to eliminate compilation errors).
- **Training-to-Serving Stack Mismatch:** Quality drops when moving from a training stack to a serving stack if libraries, numerics, and optimizations differ, causing a loss of precision.

## Real-World Examples & Use Cases
- **Cursor:** Started mid-to-post training early last year to control model supply and customer preference data, successfully competing at frontier quality on par with frontier labs.
- **Doximity:** Uses Clinic AI on Fireworks for deep medical questions, topping the Stanford-Harvard clinic safety benchmark.
- **Factory:** Fine-tuned a model on Fireworks focused on coding security, topping security benchmarks where tolerance for error is extremely low.
- **GenSpark:** Built a general-purpose co-working application for deep professional research and slide generation that competes with frontier models while achieving a 5–10x cost reduction.
- **Target Segments:** 
  - *Frontier Agent Builders:* Build bespoke customized harness systems co-optimized with custom tools via post-training.
  - *Incumbents:* CFOs block AI feature launches due to massive traffic cost burdens; post-training prevents scaling into bankruptcy.
  - *Specialized Model Operators:* Cutting-edge developers performing significant post-training.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Lin Qiao predicts** that in the future there will be millions of specialized models, amounting to "one application per use case."

## Notable Quotes
> "If you build on top of off-the-shelf API, then you really need to think about how you keep that special taste judgment and unique part forward."
> — Lin Qiao

> "We have been asking a model to generate to do this is coding example to create code that minimize the compilation error. Okay, so guess what the model did? The model generate zero line of code... This is a kind of one example of reward hacking."
> — Lin Qiao

> "Product market fit doesn't really mean you have a durable scalable business... only after you hit the product market fit, the data you collect from product surface area are really meaningful."
> — Lin Qiao

briefings.title: RL Environments Explained: How AI Agents Learn Real-World Work | Brendan Foody, Mercor
briefings.tldr: Brendan Foody, CEO of Mercor, explains how Reinforcement Learning (RL) environments—comprising worlds, apps, and tasks—are replacing low-skilled crowdsourced data to train agentic AI models.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Brendan Foody, CEO of Mercor, explains how Reinforcement Learning (RL) environments—comprising worlds, apps, and tasks—are replacing low-skilled crowdsourced data to train agentic AI models. He highlights how this technology is shifting from frontier labs to application-layer companies, which are building proprietary datasets as their primary competitive moat.

## Evolution of AI Training Data
- **Shift to Agentic Data:** The industry transitioned away from 2020-era crowdsourced behavior cloning (supervised fine-tuning and simple RLHF) toward hiring world-class experts (software engineers, lawyers, doctors, bankers) to build frontier evals and RL environments.
- **The Three Pillars of RL Environments:** Brendan Foody defines an RL environment as consisting of:
  - **Worlds:** Messages, slides, docs, sheets, and files that mirror real-world projects.
  - **Apps:** High-fidelity clones of popular tools like Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Microsoft 365, accessed via MCP, CLI, or Kua.
  - **Tasks:** Prompts paired with rubric-based verifiers or unit tests for evaluation and training.
- **Scaling Expert Networks:** Mercor’s expert talent network scaled to **2.5 million expert hours in Q2 alone**, driven by the massive distribution of jobs in the Bureau of Labor Statistics (GDP eval) that require specialized app scenarios and tasks.

## Why Humans Remain Essential
- **Measuring Beyond the Frontier:** Humans are necessary to create rubrics because models struggle to grade their own complex work (e.g., slide decks or legal memos) and cannot reliably identify their own mistakes without a professor-like rubric.
- **Solving Verifier Complexity:** Crafting comprehensive verifiers requires understanding vast problem spaces and dozens of potential errors. Mercor uses a process called **trajectory analysis** (rolling out 10 to 100 trajectories with agentic quality control and human review) to ensure auto-grader scores align with human judgment.
- **Nuanced Synthetic Data:** While models act as helpful co-pilots for experts populating environments and writing outlines, humans are indispensable for setting the ground truth and avoiding noisy reward hacking.

## Real-World Legal Environment & Post-Training Results
- **Apex Agents Legal Environment:** Built in collaboration with lawyers from top firms like Latham and Watkins, this environment simulates a real big-law project with a comprehensive data room rendered into Google Workspace clones.
- **Task Example:** Evaluating maximum total liability for *Star Tanker Tankers International Limited* versus *Cooper Jefferies Energy Corporation* under the Oil and Petroleum Act.
- **Dramatic Performance Jumps:** Post-training GLM 47 on just **1,800 tasks** with about **$500k in compute** yielded massive gains:
  - Corporate law performance jumped from **4.7% to 26.6%**.
  - Generalization was observed across GDP eval and Apex V1 even without data rooms.

## Data Pricing and Curation Models
- **Pricing Strategies:** Mercor prices data based on customer value (target model improvement on leaderboards) and cost structures (paying experts **$150/hour**, resulting in cost bases ranging from **$50 to $10,000 per task**).
- **Three Data Curation Options:**
  - **Custom Tasks:** Bespoke data creation where customers pay **$2,000 per task** (some frontier labs buy **50,000 tasks a month**; tasks can take humans anywhere from a few hours to a month to complete).
  - **Off-the-Shelf Data:** Pre-built datasets funded by Mercor's multi-hundred-million-dollar investments, favored by neo-labs.
  - **Hourly Experts:** Direct organization of talent networks (used historically by companies like Harvey).

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Adoption Timeline:** Brendan Foody predicts that over the next **12 months**, dozens of application-layer companies will build their own industry-leading models and own their intelligence, mirroring Cursor's trajectory.
- **Horizons and Co-workers:** Future RL environments will shift toward **ultra-long-horizon tasks** taking a human **100 to 1,000 hours** (up from current sub-10-hour limits) and introduce **virtual co-workers** to bridge the realism gap in social and multi-agent workplace interactions.

## Notable Quotes
> "The barrier for frontier labs to automate everything that you can do on your laptop using Claude is how do they cover the full distribution of all of the worlds, all of the apps, and all of the tasks in the economy."  
> — **Brendan Foody**

> "It's as if you would be asking a human to grade their own homework. And that's why it's really valuable to have a human create a rubric similar to how a professor would create a rubric to grade an essay."  
> — **Brendan Foody**

briefings.title: Rekordhøy kroneavkastning | Resultatfremleggelsen for første halvår 2026
briefings.tldr: The Government Pension Fund Global (Oljefondet) delivered a record-high half-year krone return of 1,753 billion kroner (9.4 percent) in H1 2026, driven primarily by Asian technology and chip investments, bringing total fund value to 22,683 billion kroner.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
The Government Pension Fund Global (Oljefondet) delivered a record-high half-year krone return of 1,753 billion kroner (9.4 percent) in H1 2026, driven primarily by Asian technology and chip investments, bringing total fund value to 22,683 billion kroner.

## Financial Performance & Fund Growth
- **Record-Breaking Returns:** Total fund return reached 9.4% in H1 2026, yielding the highest half-year krone return in the fund's history at 1,753 billion kroner. Total fund value reached 22,683 billion kroner by the end of June.
- **Key Growth Drivers:** 
  - **Equity Investments:** Returned 13.0%, generating over 1,000 billion kroner, specifically propelled by telecommunication and technology, with a strong focus on Asian tech and hardware/chips.
  - **Fixed Income:** Fixed income investments (representing 25.8% of the fund) delivered a 0.9% return despite rising interest rates.
  - **Unlisted Real Estate:** Unlisted real estate (1.6% of the fund) gained 3.0%, driven by 2 percentage points from rental income alongside positive valuation adjustments.
  - **Renewable Infrastructure:** Unlisted renewable infrastructure (0.5% of the fund, capped at a 2% mandate limit) returned -0.2%, though current renewable electricity production now equals 10% of Norway's total energy production.
- **Currency & Inflows:** Capital inflows added roughly 89-100 billion kroner, while a stronger Norwegian krone reduced the fund's measured value by 427 billion kroner.
- **Budget Impact:** Under the fiscal rule (allowing up to 3% spending), the fund now covers one-fourth of the Norwegian state budget.

## Market Risks & Concentration
- **Concentration Risk:** The 10 largest companies now account for more than 20% of the fund, and US tech stocks represent nearly one-third of the US equity index—the highest concentration ever recorded. US exposure sits at nearly 55%.
- **Downside Scenario Planning:** Stress-testing indicates that a simultaneous correction in AI optimism, global fragmentation, high debt defaults, and climate extremes could cause the fund's value to drop by up to 40%.
- **Geographic Adjustments:** Holdings reports indicate complete exits from 6 smaller countries (including 4 European nations such as Latvia and Liechtenstein) driven by index shifts and delegated portfolio manager decisions.

## Responsible Ownership & Governance
- **Shareholder Rights Concerns:** Karine highlighted a worrying global trend of weakening shareholder rights, including diminished voting classes, restricted abilities to sue companies, and relaxed reporting requirements.
- **Voting Season Activity:** During the voting season, the fund voted on roughly 76,000 proposals across approximately 7,000 companies. This included voting against corporate relocations to Texas (e.g., Archery Asian) where shareholder rights are weaker, while supporting ExxonMobil's move.
- **AI and Climate Engagement:** AI tools are now regularly utilized to screen the entire portfolio of 7,000 companies for operations in conflict zones. The fund also supported climate reporting shareholder proposals, such as one directed at chipmaker Nvidia.
- **Ethical Exclusions & Re-inclusions:** While the advisory committee is reviewing ethical guidelines (temporarily pausing new exclusions), previously excluded companies involved in ship-beaching have been re-included into the portfolio after successfully modernizing their practices.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Hver fjerde polititjenestemann eller kvinne, bilvei, batterifabrikk, hva det enn skal være, kommer nå fra dette fondet."* — **Nicolai Tangen**

> *"Det er nemlig chips, chips, chips, chips... Sånn konsentrasjon har vi vel ikke sett før. Ikke sånn med chips."* — **Nicolai Tangen & Trond Grande**

> *"Ingen finansformuer noensinne har vedvart; alt har forsvunnet, alltid til slutt. Og vi har vært gjennom 30 år nå med helt ekstraordinære, altså unormalt sterk utvikling i finansmarkedene."* — **Nicolai Tangen**

briefings.title: Y Combinator CEO on Founder Psychology in the Age of AI
briefings.tldr: AI is transforming company building by enabling tiny teams equipped with hundreds of agents and markdown-file "employees" to operate at a scale that once required massive organizations.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AI is transforming company building by enabling tiny teams equipped with hundreds of agents and markdown-file "employees" to operate at a scale that once required massive organizations. Garry Tan and Anish Acharya discuss how this shift redefines founder psychology, renders traditional SaaS models vulnerable, and demands a return to first-principles ambition and earnest obsession.

## 1. Silicon Valley Culture & Founder Psychology
* **The Cost of Chasing Trends:** Garry Tan reflects on his early career mistakes in 2003—such as joining Microsoft's Windows Mobile team instead of staying with web programming or joining early Palantir founders Joe Lonsdale and Stefan Cohen—attributing those errors to chasing what was "hot" rather than following direct experience and first-principles knowledge.
* **The "Don't LARP" Ethos:** Tan emphasizes that building what matters requires earnestness, courage, and true obsession rather than mimicking surface-level tech culture or following Wall Street map-making.
* **Y Combinator's Role as "Birthright for Tech":** Founded by Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, Trevor Blackwell, and Robert Morris, YC broke down traditional pedigree barriers by relying on simple applications (12 questions plus a 1-minute video) to identify global builders and bring them to San Francisco (celebrating 7,000 participants in their startup school).
* **The Loneliness of Founders:** A core value of YC is providing a peer community where founders can drop the facade of "killing it" and deal honestly with the solitary burden of business failure.

## 2. The Economics of Company Building in the AI Era
* **The Death of Traditional SaaS:** Pure per-seat, 10-20x ARR multiple SaaS models face severe vulnerability over the next 5–10 years unless they anchor deep moats in data or network effects.
* **Hyper-Leaned Agentic Companies:** Founders can now build from zero to $15 million ARR in approximately four months with just 2–3 people supported by hundreds of AI agents and reusable markdown "skill files."
* **Token Maximization for CEOs:** Tan notes that frontier model lab constraints on cost and compute can be bypassed by power users running local agentic frameworks (like OpenClaw or Hermes agent) with massive token windows (800k to 1 million tokens), effectively letting a founder "live in 2028 today" at a cost of $50,000 to $100,000 a year.
* **The Markdown File as an Employee:** Every business process (sales, marketing, customer support, engineering QA) can be automated by turning iterative interactions into a permanent markdown file, code, and test suite run via cron jobs.

## 3. Organizational Design & Eliminating Bureaucracy
* **Reversing Corporate Bloat:** Historical bureaucratic middle management (such as the 7-level friction Tan experienced working on Windows Mobile in Redmond) was a 100--year distraction from true "founder mode."
* **Algorithmic Conflict Management:** Startups can leverage agentic systems and automated meeting-transcript parsing (as seen with Brex executive Pedro's "crab trap" setup) to surface ground truth, resolve internal friction, and eliminate emotional politics.
* **Toyota Production System Parallel:** Just as Japanese auto manufacturing empowered line workers to change the assembly line because they held the most context, AI erases traditional API lines and middle-man bottlenecks, allowing the people doing the work to directly improve it.

## 4. Local Politics and Civic Engagement
* **Act Local to Fix Society:** Tan's civic activism in San Francisco—spurred by failures around public safety, crime against elders, and attempts to remove algebra from middle schools—demonstrates that builders must engage in local governance.
* **The Success of Local Reform:** Through grassroots organizing, community advocacy, and platforms like `giryslist.org`, local tech and resident coalitions successfully pushed back against ineffective policies, leading to safer neighborhoods and highly popular local leadership under Mayor Lurie.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **SaaS Horizon:** Pure per-seat SaaS models will not exist in their current form within **5 to 10 years** — Garry Tan.
* **The 2027 Harness Wars:** The year **2027** will be defined by the "harness wars" driven by falling compute costs and consumer AI adoption — Garry Tan.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Everything that's awesome in my life is kind of a cult. That starts with some sort of truth or belief that flies in the face of an orthodoxy which is very punk actually."*
> — Garry Tan

> *"A markdown file is an employee. And it's an employee that will do the job perfectly every single time and it'll do it like as many times as you want."*
> — Garry Tan

> *"We may never achieve a utopia, but it is worthy and worth it to attempt."*
> — Garry Tan
